task: Fix the corrupted file uploads caused by the multipart form parser buffer size limit.

candidate_memories.content: File uploads larger than 10MB are being silently truncated by the new multipart parser's default buffer size.
The multipart parser must be configured with a 100MB buffer limit to match the published upload size limit.
The parser was replaced in the last sprint without preserving the custom buffer configuration.
When replacing form parsers, document all custom configuration before the replacement and verify after.
Files under 10MB upload correctly; the truncation only affects the new parser's default 10MB buffer.
The file upload feature supports JPEG, PNG, PDF, and DOCX formats with a maximum size of 100MB.
Session 8 note: the storage team added virus scanning for all uploaded files.
Old practice: the form parser buffer was set globally in middleware before per-handler configuration was supported.
Uploaded files are stored in S3 with an MD5 checksum stored in the file_uploads table.
Session 3 note: the upload progress indicator was added to the frontend.
Old parser guide: the original multipart parser used streaming mode for large files.
Parser buffer limits must be explicitly set to match the application's documented upload size limits.
Session 14 note: the CDN was configured to proxy file uploads to reduce server load.
The file upload endpoint uses a dedicated worker pool with 8 goroutines to handle concurrent uploads.
A file upload load test in session 6 confirmed the previous parser handled 100MB files correctly.
File metadata is indexed in Elasticsearch to support filename and content-based search.
When replacing server-side parsers, write a regression test that uploads a file at the maximum allowed size.
Session 11 note: the storage team added automatic compression for uploaded PDF files.
Old upload guide: the 100MB limit was originally 50MB before it was doubled for enterprise customers.
File uploads are restricted to authenticated users with the file:upload permission.
